ENGLISH                                        This section contains 11 questions.
                                               The time allotted is 20 minutes.

The following section contains three types of questions: Sentence Completion, Restatement
and Reading Comprehension. Each question is followed by four possible responses. Choose
the response which best answers the question and mark its number in the appropriate place
on the answer sheet.

Sentence Completions (Questions 1-3)

This part consists of sentences with a word or words missing in each. For each question,
choose the answer which best completes the sentence.

1. A good fixture helps a parser         hidden regressions.

(1) detect
(2) forbid
(3) praise
(4) recall

2. The invented sample text is the        of the real exam layout.

(1) forecaster
(2) mirror
(3) inspector
(4) publisher

                                     9

3. Test suites          before a release, not after one.

(1) run
(2) bury
(3) delay
(4) ignore

Restatements (Questions 4-5)

This part consists of several sentences, each followed by four possible ways of restating
the main idea of that sentence in different words.

4. The parser strips page footers before it looks for questions.

(1) Footers are removed first, then questions are found.
(2) Questions are found first, then footers are removed.
(3) Footers are never removed from the extracted text.
(4) Questions and footers are found at the same time.

5. Every option in a question must survive the cleanup step.

(1) Cleanup may drop some options.
(2) No option should be lost during cleanup.
(3) Options are added during cleanup.
(4) Cleanup applies only to stems.

Reading Comprehension

This part consists of two passages, each followed by several related questions.

Text I (Questions 6-8)

(1) This passage is invented prose written only to exercise the parser. It is laid out
       in numbered lines the way the extracted exam text is, so that the numbering is
(5) stripped from the passage body when it is joined into a paragraph.
(10) The passage also contains an em dash � to check that the replacement character
       produced by the text extractor is turned back into a real dash.

Questions

6. The main purpose of the first paragraph is to -

       (1) describe the fixture
       (2) describe the parser
       (3) describe the exam
       (4) describe the dash

7. According to the passage, the line numbers are -

       (1) kept in place
       (2) stripped out
       (3) turned into dashes
       (4) counted

8. The passage suggests that the replacement character is -

       (1) left alone
       (2) deleted
       (3) restored to a dash
       (4) doubled

Text II (Questions 9-11)

(1) A second invented passage follows the first one so that both reading passages in a
       section are covered by the fixture.
(2) It is deliberately short.

Questions

9. The second passage exists in order to -

       (1) cover a second passage
       (2) cover a second section
       (3) cover the answer key
       (4) cover the footer

10. The second passage is described as -

       (1) long
       (2) short
       (3) missing
       (4) numbered

11. Both passages belong to -

       (1) the same section
       (2) different sections
       (3) the answer key
       (4) the appendix

ENGLISH                                        This section contains 11 questions.
                                               The time allotted is 20 minutes.

The following section contains three types of questions: Sentence Completion, Restatement
and Reading Comprehension. Each question is followed by four possible responses. Choose
the response which best answers the question and mark its number in the appropriate place
on the answer sheet.

Sentence Completions (Questions 1-3)

This part consists of sentences with a word or words missing in each.

1. The second section repeats the         of the first one.

(1) structure
(2) footer
(3) appendix
(4) dash

2. Question numbering          in each section.

(1) restarts
(2) continues
(3) stops
(4) reverses

3. Each answer key row covers one          .

(1) section
(2) passage
(3) option
(4) page

Restatements (Questions 4-5)

This part consists of several sentences.

4. The answer key is stored as one digit per question.

(1) One digit stands for one question.
(2) One digit stands for one section.
(3) Digits are unrelated to questions.
(4) Each question has four digits.

5. Both sections are parsed with the same code path.

(1) The sections use different parsers.
(2) The sections share a parser.
(3) Only the first section is parsed.
(4) Only the second section is parsed.

Reading Comprehension

This part consists of two passages, each followed by several related questions.
